# University of the Andes (Colombia): Summary
The University of the Andes (Colombia), founded in 1948 and beginning classes in March 1949, was established as the first nonsectarian and politically independent university in Colombia. Modeled after the American university system, Uniandes aimed to educate professionals with technical and liberal knowledge to support national development. Despite early challenges and political unrest, the university maintained neutrality and promoted academic excellence, interdisciplinary study, and international collaboration—such as exchange programs with American universities and active recruitment of foreign faculty. The academic structure allows students flexibility in curricular choices, supported by a four-cycle system blending professional, socio-humanistic, and elective courses. Uniandes is recognized for fostering pluralism, dialogue, and social responsibility among its students.
Administratively, Uniandes operates as a nonprofit corporation with substantial autonomy, governed by a Board of Trustees, Board of Directors, Rector, and other academic bodies. The university includes 10 faculties and several academic centers, served by a highly qualified faculty (70% with doctorates from top global universities). With assets totaling over $426 million as of 2020, the campus in Bogotá features renovated industrial and religious buildings alongside modern facilities, extensive libraries, laboratories, sports centers, and strong technological infrastructure. Uniandes has an active international exchange program with over 119 partner universities. Its notable alumni include leaders in government, the arts, sciences, and academia, underscoring its role as a premier Colombian institution for higher education and research.
